findings.evidence: restart() performs launchd._launchd_bootout(wait_timeout=T), optional _terminate_daemon_processes(timeout=T), then _wait_for_daemon(timeout=T) sequentially. _launchctl has its own 10-second timeout; unload polling can overshoot its deadline by one such call, and bootstrap may fall back to legacy load.
findings.impact: A watchdog sized only as T+10 or 2*T+10 can terminate valid restart progress before the CLI's own bounded phases finish.
findings.required_refinement: Allow three readiness-sized phases plus conservative launchctl/process overhead in the desktop restart watchdog. A simple 3*T+120-second outer guard is reasonable here; document it as a guard with margin, not an exact global upper bound for arbitrary process discovery. Start has one readiness-sized phase plus process overhead. Do not change CLI phase semantics or add another readiness framework.

acceptance_review.requirement: One named desktop readiness default of 60 seconds used by startDaemon, restartDaemon, ensureDaemonReady and the restart calls inside installOrRepair and repairPreparedInstall. Existing install-command 240/180-second budgets and status probe limits are separate operations and should not be reduced to 60.

acceptance_review.criterion: Preserve explicit CLI and service caller timeout semantics
acceptance_review.requirement: Do not change Python CLI default/options or silently replace explicit numeric/options timeouts on direct service calls. Desktop 60 seconds is a per-readiness-phase default, not the total install/restart deadline.

acceptance_review.criterion: Preserve truthful failure handling and one restart
acceptance_review.requirement: Keep immediate failure on genuine nonzero child exit; do not upgrade failed restart to success because a later health probe sees another process. One install/repair attempt invokes one restart; bootstrap failure, port blocker and readiness timeout remain failures.

acceptance_review.criterion: Reproduce the actual regression in the existing harness
acceptance_review.requirement: Exercise actual installOrRepair/prepareInstalledVersion with mock child/timer behavior representing health at 26 seconds. Old 20-second deadline must fail, new default must succeed without a second restart. Prove readiness and prepared-marker update; prove Doctor in forced/runDoctor=true flow. Preserve existing automatic prepare runDoctor=false policy. Verify the next current-install startup skips a full repeated install.

Verify a CLI consuming legitimate sequential stop/start phases is not killed by the outer guard. Verify explicit short timeout, never-ready, bootstrap/nonzero failure and port blocker do not produce a prepared marker or successful readiness. Reuse CLI regressions for unchanged ownership/restoration behavior rather than reimplementing it in JS.

Keep repair in canonical desktop service.js, focused existing test harness and affected lifecycle docs. No fallback owner, registry, new mode, new CLI abstraction, or unconditional Doctor behavior is needed.
